FR-001.title: The authoring experience MUST let an Overseer define reusable facility devices with a stable identity, display name, device kind, authored initial state, current state, and a finite set of named states.

FR-002.title: Each facility device transition MUST identify one device, one allowed source state, one destination state, and an authored transition name.

FR-003.title: Facility validation MUST reject duplicate identities, duplicate state names within a device, unknown initial states, and transitions whose source or destination does not belong to the device.

FR-004.title: Facility devices and their current states MUST be owned by the session-wide facility rather than by a terminal or terminal group.

FR-005.title: Moving a terminal between groups MUST NOT clone, reset, delete, or retarget any facility device or reference.

FR-006.title: A terminal command MUST be able to request one or more authored device transitions as one world action through the existing private approval lifecycle.

FR-007.title: A requested world action MUST NOT mutate device state, condition state, saved revisions, or state-driven presentation before approval.

FR-008.title: Rejection or dismissal of a requested player world action MUST leave facility state unchanged and MUST reuse the current authoritative access-error presentation with an explicit rejected result.

FR-009.title: Approval MUST revalidate every requested device, transition, expected source state, precondition, and relevant revision against the current canonical facility state.

FR-010.title: A multi-device world action MUST apply all requested transitions or leave every affected device unchanged.

FR-011.title: A successful world action MUST advance the canonical facility revision once and MUST perform at most one durable commit.

FR-012.title: A persistence failure MUST leave the prior facility state authoritative and MUST NOT publish a successful result or partial projection.

FR-013.title: Repeated decisions for the same correlated request MUST NOT produce more than one committed world action.

FR-014.title: Concurrent world actions with overlapping affected devices MUST serialize through the centralized player-action transaction so at most one action can commit from the same expected state.

FR-015.title: Missing references, invalid transitions, failed preconditions, stale revisions, conflicts, and persistence failures MUST return stable structured failure categories with safe affected identities.

FR-016.title: Facility failure handling MUST NOT depend on matching human-readable error message text.

FR-017.title: An Overseer MUST be able to bind a menu label variant to equality between one device and one known state.

FR-018.title: An Overseer MUST be able to bind an EntryContent block variant to equality between one device and one known state.

FR-019.title: An Overseer MUST be able to bind command availability to equality between one device and one known state.

FR-020.title: An Overseer MUST be able to bind simple content visibility to equality between one device and one known state.

FR-021.title: Authoring validation MUST reject a presentation or behavior condition whose compared state does not belong to its referenced device.

FR-022.title: Connected player and Overseer presentations MUST refresh state-driven labels, blocks, availability, and visibility from the newly committed facility state without requiring session reload.

FR-023.title: When a facility binding and a completed-command snapshot affect the same presentation property, the facility binding MUST determine that property's effective value.

FR-024.title: The existing completed-command result and completion lifecycle MUST remain authoritative for command-result presentation even when that command also requests facility transitions.

FR-025.title: Device-driven content MUST be derived from canonical facility state and authored variants rather than persisted as another completed-command snapshot.

FR-026.title: A diagnostic condition MUST have a stable identity, authored category, affected terminal or device, authored initial status, current status, and explicitly selected effects.

FR-027.title: The authored diagnostic categories MUST include offline, unpowered, network-isolated, storage-damaged, authorization-corrupted, and display-unstable conditions, and MUST allow additional named authored faults with the same bounded behavior model.

FR-028.title: A diagnostic condition MUST be able to block explicitly selected capabilities without changing unrelated capabilities.

FR-029.title: A diagnostic condition MUST be able to expose an authored diagnostic menu or diagnostic content path.

FR-030.title: A diagnostic condition MUST be able to select authored partial-record variants without randomly deleting or permanently altering source content.

FR-031.title: Repeated rendering of the same facility and condition state MUST produce the same content, visibility, availability, and navigation result.

FR-032.title: Visual corruption or instability effects MUST NOT mutate facility state, condition state, authored content, or durable session data merely because an effect plays.

FR-033.title: Recovery from an active condition MUST occur only through an approved authored device transition, a compatible authored holotape program, or a confirmed private Overseer action.

FR-034.title: A compatible holotape recovery program MUST be limited to selecting authored recovery actions and MUST NOT execute arbitrary scripts or expressions.

FR-035.title: Approved device states, condition states, and facility revisions MUST persist across broadcast stop, application restart, supported self-update, and session reload.

FR-036.title: Pending world-action approvals MUST be transient and MUST become incapable of committing after their broadcast, session, or application runtime context ends.

FR-037.title: The Overseer MUST be able to inspect every direct dependency on a selected device, state, transition, or condition before changing its identity or deleting it.

FR-038.title: Previewing a device state or condition MUST NOT change canonical state, revisions, pending approvals, saved data, or connected player presentation.

FR-039.title: A confirmed single-device reset MUST restore that device and its device-scoped conditions to authored initial values in one facility revision without changing unrelated devices.

FR-040.title: A confirmed whole-facility reset MUST restore all devices and diagnostic conditions to authored initial values through one atomic durable commit.

FR-041.title: A failed reset MUST leave all device states, condition states, revisions, and player projections at their last committed values.

FR-042.title: Every player presentation affected by device state or diagnostic conditions MUST retain an authoritative escape path, and the Overseer MUST retain a private recovery action when authored restrictions make normal player progress unusable.

FR-043.title: The Overseer interface MUST support creating, editing, validating, and inspecting devices, states, transitions, conditions, references, and recovery paths without manual JSON editing.

FR-044.title: Deleting or changing the stable identity of a referenced facility entity MUST be blocked until every affected reference is explicitly removed, repaired, or reassigned.

FR-045.title: An explicit multi-reference repair or reassignment MUST save all selected reference changes together or leave every reference unchanged.

FR-046.title: Changing a facility entity's display name while preserving its stable identity MUST preserve its current state, transitions, conditions, and references.

FR-047.title: Publication of authored facility changes MUST validate the complete affected reference and recovery graph before those changes become available to players.

FR-048.title: Facility requests, approvals, rejections, transitions, structured failures, and resets MUST emit retained runtime-log records with a shared correlation identity for each action.

FR-049.title: Facility log records MUST identify safe device identities, action category, outcome category, and relevant facility revisions without recording authored labels, content, secrets, or raw private errors.

FR-050.title: Retained logs MUST remain diagnostic evidence and MUST NOT be read as a source for facility state, replay, recovery, or conflict resolution.

FR-051.title: Ordinary commands, legacy state-changing commands, terminal transitions, hacking, player roles, and existing command-driven EntryContent completion behavior MUST remain usable without facility configuration.

intent: Give tabletop sessions one durable, shared, authorable facility state whose approved atomic changes project consistently across every terminal.
expectations: No arbitrary scripting or general expression language.
No random hardware degradation or nondeterministic fault activation.
No permanent destruction of authored content.
No combat resolution or automatic repair-success determination.
No smart-lighting integration, physical smoke control, or scene-cue automation.
approach: Persist one optional session-wide facility in JSON v1; extend state-changing commands so command completion and all device or condition changes use one coordinator-held atomic store call; derive every terminal presentation from the saved facility through one pure evaluator.

decisions.decision: Keep facility authority in the version-1 session
decisions.why: It already owns durable campaign state and atomic replacement.
decisions.rejected: A separate facility file or runtime logs.

decisions.decision: Keep document, facility, and coordination revisions distinct
decisions.why: Each protects durable storage, world-action staleness, or publication ordering.
decisions.rejected: Reusing one revision for all boundaries.

decisions.decision: Extend existing state-changing commands with facility actions
decisions.why: It preserves the approval and immutable completion lifecycle.
decisions.rejected: A new command behavior or approval system.

decisions.decision: Commit completion and facility transitions in one store operation
decisions.why: One candidate and one atomic write prevent split state.

decisions.decision: Use one global persistent facility revision
decisions.why: Strict total ordering makes stale and concurrent requests deterministic.

decisions.decision: Use one pure evaluator for authorization and projection
decisions.why: Server decisions and rendered state cannot drift.

decisions.decision: Apply base, completion, device, then diagnostic precedence
decisions.why: The order preserves legacy snapshots and deterministic authored faults.

decisions.decision: Model diagnostics as bounded typed condition effects
decisions.why: Conditions share facility persistence and cannot become executable expressions.
decisions.rejected: Random faults or a separate diagnostics store.

decisions.decision: Model holotape recovery as allowlisted authored programs
decisions.why: No holotape subsystem exists and bounded selectors avoid scripting.
decisions.rejected: A runtime interpreter or deferring recovery compatibility.

decisions.decision: Use typed private failures and the existing player access-error view
decisions.why: Stable codes support repair and logs while preserving player navigation.
decisions.rejected: Message-text matching or a second player error surface.

decisions.decision: Partition the 1000-attempt coordinator stress matrix into four 250-attempt cases
decisions.why: This directly covers committed duplicate retries, stale identities, disjoint multi-device actions, and overlapping approvals while retaining exact write-count and final-state assertions.
decisions.rejected: One homogeneous retry loop that could not distinguish the required request classes.

decisions.decision: Replay every diagnostic category through both the pure projector and detached preview path
decisions.why: The two outputs jointly cover capability, content, effects, navigation, authored inputs, completed-command state, and persistent facility immutability.

decisions.decision: Treat the two Overseer demo members as local and remote views of one console
decisions.why: Constitution IX requires members of one group to preserve one in-world terminal identity and ordered access-context transitions.
decisions.rejected: Grouping independent machines by building or narrative location.

decisions.decision: Place every independent demo machine in its own terminal group
decisions.why: The greenhouse, lift, security post, and ATLAS relay are separate installations even where locations are related.
decisions.rejected: Using terminal groups as building or department containers.

decisions.decision: Keep initial/current facility deltas and completed command snapshots in the canonical demo
decisions.why: One portable session can visibly demonstrate persistence, bound projections, and reset behavior while the inventory gives exact recovery steps.
decisions.rejected: A pristine demo that hides completed and changed-state branches.

decisions.decision: Forward the facility browser fixture through the complete terminal lifecycle interface
decisions.why: The fixture must preserve authoritative replacement and navigation semantics while layering deterministic facility projections.
decisions.rejected: Suppressing the failing grouping and navigation browser coverage.

decisions.decision: Retain Wails v2 and beta.8 references only as labeled historical evidence
decisions.why: The accepted runtime is beta.15 and completed migrations cannot remain active rollback authority.
decisions.rejected: Keeping Wails v2 as a current production fallback.
